lessons.title: Flow types are not one canvas
lessons.why: Each flow type only offers the blocks that make sense there. A hold flow is not a place to transfer to a queue and hope.
paras: Inbound flows greet and route. Customer queue flows run while the customer waits and can offer a callback. Hold flows loop prompts. Whisper flows play just before the join. Transfer-to-agent and transfer-to-queue flows are what quick connects run. Disconnect flows run after the end.
Outbound whisper flows are where you set outbound recording and where Call phone number belongs.
points: A customer queue flow is interruptible.
Transfer to queue inside a customer queue flow moves a contact that is already queued.
End flow / Resume ends the flow and does not hang up.
Disconnect hangs up.
lessons.mistake: Putting the hold music in the inbound flow and wondering why hold is silent.

number.n: Inbound, queue, hold, whisper, transfer, disconnect, outbound

lessons.title: The block catalog, grouped by job
lessons.why: You do not memorize fifty icons. You group them by the job they do.
paras: Control blocks move the contact: Play prompt, Get customer input, Distribute by percentage, Loop, Wait, Transfer to flow, End flow, Disconnect. Data blocks read and write attributes, metrics, profiles, cases, and data tables. Routing blocks set the queue, the criteria, the priority, and then transfer.

Integration blocks call Lambda, Lex through Get customer input, a module, an external tool, or an AI agents domain. The full list in the designer is the source of truth. This campus includes every block from that list in the lab palette and the glossary.
points: Check hours, Check queue status, Check staffing, and Get metrics are how a flow refuses work it cannot staff.
Set logging and Set recording are how you can prove what happened.
Show view is the step-by-step guide.
Agentic CX and Connect assistant are the 2026 AI entry points. Voice ID blocks remain on the list and should not be added. Support ended 20 May 2026.
lessons.mistake: Using a block because it is visible, including Voice ID.

lessons.title: Attributes are the only memory the next system gets
lessons.why: If it is not an attribute, the CRM, the whisper, and the CTR cannot see it.
paras: Set contact attributes writes strings. Check contact attributes branches on them. Lambda and Lex write them too. Names are case-sensitive in practice. Pick a prefix for your company and do not collide with system attributes.
The screen pop, the case field, and the WFM code all want the same customer id. Write it once, early, before any transfer.
points: System attributes include the queue, the channel, and the customer endpoint.
Lex exposes intent and slots. Copy the ones you care about into your own names.
A transfer to another flow keeps the contact attributes.
A transfer to a phone number leaves Connect. Attributes do not ride the PSTN.
lessons.mistake: Asking the customer for an account number and never storing it.

lessons.title: Modules are how you stop copying flows
lessons.why: A copied inbound flow drifts. A module has one published body.
paras: Invoke module runs a published module. Return (from module) ends it successfully. The default quota is 200 modules. Inputs and outputs should be attributes you have named, not a comment in the designer.
Global Resiliency replicates modules. A module that calls a Lambda in only one Region will fail in the other Region unless the function is there too.
points: Publish, then invoke. A draft module is not what production runs.
Keep authentication, language selection, and recording policy in modules.
Version the module in your stack as ContactFlowModule JSON.
Test the module with the same error branches as a flow.
lessons.mistake: Fixing a bug in one of eight copied flows.

lessons.title: Every error branch is a product decision
lessons.why: An unconnected error output hangs up. That is a choice, even if you did not mean it.
paras: Lambda has Success, Error, and, when synchronous, Timeout. Lex and Get customer input have error and timeout paths. Hours have in and out. Transfers have capacity and error paths. Connect each one to a prompt a human would accept.
Distribute by percentage is for a measured pilot. It is not a skills router. Loop can spin. Cap it.
points: Turn logging on before the first test call.
The disconnect flow does not save you from an error hang-up. The customer is already gone.
Wait and Play prompt are how you avoid silence during async Lambda.
Touchtone buffer lets callers type ahead. Turn it on only if the prompts allow it.
lessons.mistake: Leaving the red error port empty because the happy path worked once.

lessons.title: The flow language is how instances share a design
lessons.why: The designer is a view. The JSON is what you review and promote.
paras: An action has a type, parameters, and transitions. Conditions can nest no more than five deep, with no more than 50 sub-conditions. Operators compare strings and numbers. A non-numeric comparison against GreaterThan returns false.
Action kinds are contact, participant, interaction, and flow control. Participant actions such as Play prompt need a participant. Some disconnect flows do not have one.
points: Use the JSON to move a flow between a test instance and production.
Do not hand-edit a 2,000-line export without a diff.
Modules have their own JSON.
The API still says Amazon Connect in places. The admin guide may say Connect Customer. The JSON types are what the API accepts.
lessons.mistake: Treating a screenshot of the designer as the source of truth.
